_readme: Ratchets for patterns that should only ever get RARER. Measured 2026-09-03 on a clean tree.
The pattern lives HERE and nowhere else -- scripts/check-count-ratchet.mjs reads it from this
file rather than carrying its own copy. That is the lesson from scripts/style-count.sh: the
style-literal pattern was duplicated six times, one copy drifted, and the generator could then
write a baseline the counter disagreed with -- failing the very commit meant to lower it.
A count RISING fails the push. A count FALLING prints a note asking for this file to be lowered;
leaving it high turns a ratchet into a permit.

Counts are measured with COMMENTS STRIPPED (scripts/lib/comments.mjs) since 2026-09-04 -- a comment mentioning a pattern is documentation, not an occurrence. Baselines were re-measured in that same commit, which is why three of them dropped.

empty-state markup.why: 35 hand-rolled empty states (counted with comments stripped). Phase 6 replaces them with one _emptyState(msg) builder; until then this stops a 36th being written.

Loading ellipsis.why: 23 copies of the same loading string (comments stripped). Same story as empty-state: a _loading() builder in Phase 6.

toLocaleDateString(.why: Ten distinct option shapes across 36 sites, which is why dates render inconsistently between pages. Phase 3 introduces fmtDateGB(dateStr, shape).

role === 'solo'.why: The solo role test, inlined 38 times in CODE (comments stripped). Every one is a place a future _isSolo() change would have to be repeated -- and solo scoping is this project's most-shipped bug class (four separate coach_id/solo bugs). Phase 3 adds _isSolo().

typeof shield.why: A load-order shield. It does not throw -- it quietly yields the fallback, so the symptom is an empty list or a missing colour with no error anywhere. Phase 5 hoists the declarations and deletes these.

waitForTimeout(.why: Fixed sleeps in the E2E suite -- pure wall-clock cost on a 35-minute run, and each one is either too short (flaky) or too long (slow). Phase 2 converts them to real waits. Raised by exactly 1 on 2026-09-16: tests/template-draft-save-2026-09-13.spec.js's partial-failure-recovery test waits out a real, un-awaited network round-trip (a propagation-triggered openTemplate() repaint) to prove openTemplate's new dirty-draft guard holds under real timing, not just a fast read beating a slow repaint -- there is no positive DOM/JS signal to poll for since the test is proving an absence (nothing changes). Raised by exactly 1 again on 2026-09-28: tests/template-editor-post-save-navigate-clobber-2026-09-28.spec.js proves the same class of abandoned repaint (this time landing after a successful Save + immediate navigate-away, not a failed one) does not clobber the page the user is actually on -- same reasoning, no positive signal to poll for.

swallowed catch.why: A .catch(() => {}) in a test hides the failure it was meant to tolerate. One of these hid a ReferenceError in program-ownership-anchors-2026-08-22.spec.js:27 for eleven days, during which that spec's cleanup never ran once and left 242 rows in the live database. Raised by exactly 2 on 2026-09-29: tests/progress.spec.js's new Goals-tab-open test opens two extra Playwright browser contexts (an insert fixture and its own cleanup, mirroring tests/goal-ownership-2026-08-21.spec.js:38-49's own ctx.close().catch(() => {}) already in this baseline) and closes each the same way. This is not the shape the cited incident warns about: it swallows a browser-context teardown failure inside a `finally`, not a DB query or assertion result, and the actual cleanup query it wraps still uses .select('id') + a rowcount check per this file's own teardown-hygiene rule, not a bare .catch(). Leaving ctx.close() unguarded would let a teardown-only rejection overwrite a real in-flight assertion failure from the same finally block, which is a worse failure mode than the one this ratchet targets. Raised by exactly 2 more on 2026-09-30, not by the diff that raised it: the RPE-autoregulation merge (a33039d) landed tests/rpe-top-set-2026-09-29.spec.js's cleanupFixture and cleanupBuilderFixture, each ending page.evaluate(...).catch(() => {}) around their own cleanup query -- same shape and same reasoning as the 2026-09-29 pair right above (a teardown-only rejection must not overwrite a real in-flight test failure), just never counted until this session's unrelated runner-UI fixes were the first commit to touch that file since the merge. Verified neither line is new code from this session's own diff.
